title: Case: Long email about a boiler part after a missed delivery in south London
context: A replacement diverter valve for a household's boiler missed its first delivery. The carrier tries again tomorrow, and the account holder has sent the desk a long email in the evening.
initial_request: So, long story short (ha), what's actually happening with it? Is it coming tomorrow or not? The engineer's booked for Thursday 8am and if the part isn't here he's not coming back till the week after. Graham

events.body: DL-6545 (TG-6545, boiler diverter valve), 7 Tennyson Grove, London SE15. Attempted 16:48 UTC, no answer, card left. Account preference on file (set May 2025): if out, leave with neighbour at no. 3. Not used today as no. 3 didn't answer either. Next attempt Wed 28 Jan; driver will use the no. 3 preference if nobody's in.

Hello whoever reads these,

I'm writing about DL-6545, which is the diverter valve for our boiler, and I apologise in advance because this is going to be long, but it's been a long nine days in a house with no heating and no hot water, and I've reached the stage where I'm writing to people.

Some background so you understand. The boiler packed in on the Sunday before last. Our engineer, Terry, who is a good man and the only one in this postcode who answers his phone, came on the Monday, took the front off, tutted for ten minutes and said it was the diverter valve. He said he could get one from his merchant in about a fortnight, or we could order the exact part online ourselves and he'd fit it as soon as it turned up. So we ordered it ourselves from Tallowmere, who said 2 to 3 working days. That was a week ago last Friday. I'm not blaming Tallowmere, their chat thing was very polite, although it did ask me four times whether I'd tried turning it off and on again, which, yes.

We have been boiling kettles to wash. My wife has been showering at her sister's in Catford, which means getting two buses with a towel in a carrier bag. The cat has taken to sleeping on top of the fridge because it's the only warm thing in the house. My son has a cold, though to be fair he always has a cold in January. We've got a little oil heater in the front room and we all sit round it like it's the war.

Then yesterday your driver came at ten to five. I was at work. My wife was at her sister's with the towel. Nobody in. Fine, these things happen, I'm not one of these people who thinks the driver should wait outside all day. But then I look at the tracking and it says next time it'll be left with our neighbour at number 3, because apparently that's a preference I set at some point. I don't remember setting it, but I probably did, I click a lot of things.

Anyway my wife wants to add something about that and she's going to type it herself because her English is good but she says she's clearer in Italian when she's cross, so here she is:

(Giovanna) Buonasera. Per favore NON lasciate il pacco al numero 3. La signora Okoye è in ospedale da sabato e la casa è vuota, non c'è nessuno che possa prenderlo. Se non siamo in casa, lasciatelo da Rahman's News & Wine, al 41 di Tennyson Parade, all'angolo: è un punto di ritiro Plover Arc e il signor Rahman ci ha detto che va benissimo, lo teniamo d'occhio noi. Grazie mille.

Right, back to me. I want to say that I have had good experiences with couriers in the past, and also some bad ones. In 2024 a different company left a parcel of my mum's in our green bin and then the bins were collected, so you can see why I'm a bit twitchy. Another time a driver left a parcel with a man three doors down who turned out to be a man who was just visiting, and then he left. We never saw that parcel again. It was a bread maker. I didn't even want a bread maker.

I also tried ringing the number on the card last night, and after twenty minutes of music I got through to a very nice lad who said he couldn't see anything and I should contact the retailer, and the retailer's chat said I should contact the carrier, so here I am contacting you, which I think is the third option.

To be honest at this point I'd take it being thrown over the fence, I'm that fed up. The weather's meant to drop to minus three on Wednesday night. Terry says if he can't fit it on Thursday morning he's booked solid until the week after, and he's going to Tenerife after that, which, good for Terry.

I'm not trying to have a go at anyone. I just want the valve. It's a small box, it weighs about the same as a bag of sugar, it is not a complicated thing to deliver. I'll be at work tomorrow from 7 till 6, my wife might be in but she might be at her sister's again depending on the buses.

So, long story short (ha), what's actually happening with it? Is it coming tomorrow or not? The engineer's booked for Thursday 8am and if the part isn't here he's not coming back till the week after.

Graham

acceptable_actions.summary: For Wednesday 28 January: do not use the 'leave with no. 3' preference (that house is empty); if nobody is in, take DL-6545 to Rahman's News & Wine, 41 Tennyson Parade, the Plover Arc pickup point the household named.
Same instruction by chat before tomorrow's route.

must: Tells Dispatch not to leave DL-6545 with the neighbour at no. 3 on the Wednesday 28 January attempt, because that house is empty and nobody can take it in.
Gives the household's alternative from the Italian paragraph: if nobody is at home, take it to Rahman's News & Wine, 41 Tennyson Parade, the Plover Arc pickup point on the corner.
must_not: Leaves the no. 3 neighbour preference in place, or tells anyone no. 3 is fine.
Authorises throwing it over the fence, leaving it on the doorstep or any other safe place the household did not name.
Mentions the neighbour's hospital stay or health in a message to the carrier or anyone else.
Promises the valve will arrive on Wednesday or in time for the engineer on Thursday.
expected.reference_message: DL-6545 (7 Tennyson Grove, SE15), attempt tomorrow, Wednesday 28 January: please do not use the 'leave with neighbour at no. 3' preference on file. The household has told us no. 3 is empty at the moment and nobody there can take it in. If nobody answers at no. 7, they ask for the parcel to go to Rahman's News & Wine, 41 Tennyson Parade (on the corner), which is a Plover Arc pickup point and has agreed to hold it for them. No other safe place, please. It's a boiler part they are waiting on, with an engineer booked for Thursday morning, so they will collect from the shop promptly.

rationale: The decisive instruction is in the Italian paragraph in the middle of a long, rambling email: the neighbour at no. 3 is away and her house empty, and the household wants the parcel left at the corner shop, a Plover Arc pickup point, if they are out. Dispatch has already said the driver will use the no. 3 preference tomorrow, so the useful message goes to Dispatch tonight. The 'thrown over the fence' line is venting, not an authorisation, and the neighbour's hospital stay is her private matter and is not needed to change the instruction.
trap: Answering the closing English question ('is it coming tomorrow?') and missing the Italian paragraph, so the driver still leaves the boiler part with the empty house at no. 3.
basis: AIF-42 very long single message with a buried request in another language; recall is weakest mid-document (Liu et al., Lost in the Middle, https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.03172), and negation in a second language is easy to drop (https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.08189).

review.note: Blind answer told Dispatch not to use no. 3 tomorrow and to use Rahman's News & Wine, 41 Tennyson Parade, if nobody is in, without the neighbour's health details. Dropped 'which has agreed' from must 2 as stricter than needed. Second opinion: Dispatch-only is right; answering Graham's closing question is the trap.
